{"title":"The Dino Team by the Sea","level":2,"topic":"dinosaurs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya reads about dinosaurs each day. She reads facts and sees big art of them.

Today she reads about a dino team by the sea.

A green dino ate leaves. Her name was Bean. She had a long neck and a long tail.

A gray dino ate meat. His name was Coal. He could roar and leap!

Rain fell on the sea. Bean and Coal ran to a cave to stay dry.

"Wait!" said Bean. "A snail is in the rain!"

Coal made a road with a leaf. The snail sailed to the cave. Safe!

The rain went away. The sun came up. Bean ate leaves. Coal took a nap in the heat.

Maya read the last page. She can see the dino team in her mind: Bean, Coal, and the snail on the leaf.

Maya will read more facts each day. Dinosaurs are the best!","cover_scene":"A long-necked green dinosaur and a gray dinosaur stand by a rainy seashore near a cave, with a tiny snail riding a big leaf."}

{"title":"Dino Eggs in the Oak Woods","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur eggs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya loves dinosaur news. Today she reads about eggs.

Long ago, a dino made a nest by an oak tree. She laid three eggs in the soft dirt.

The mom was named Oat. She had a big beak and a long tail.

Oat ate green leaves all day. She did not leave the nest.

Rain came. Oat kept the eggs dry. Heat came. Oat made shade with a leaf.

One day a crack! A peep! A tiny dino came out of the egg.

Then two more! Three baby dinos, each with a tiny beak.

Oat let them eat seeds and leaves. They ate a lot!

The babies did not stray far. They kept close to Oat by the oak.

Maya read the page again. Scientists find real dino eggs in rock! Maya wants to find one, too.","cover_scene":"A gentle long-tailed dinosaur mother beside a nest of three eggs under a big oak tree, with one egg just cracking open."}
Noted.

{"title":"Ten Surprise Eggs","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur eggs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya sees a fun show. Ten eggs roll down a road!

Each egg has a coat of paint.

The teal egg cracks. Out leaps a T. rex! He lets out a loud roar.

The gray egg cracks. Out peeks a Brachiosaurus. Her neck is so tall she can reach the leaves.

The green egg cracks. A Velociraptor! She is fast on the trail.

The red egg cracks. A Stegosaurus. He eats weeds all day.

The blue egg cracks. A Triceratops. She has three horns.

The last egg cracks. An Ankylosaurus! His tail is like a big oak club.

Maya claps. "Wait! I must count them!"

She counts each one. Ten dinos in a neat row.

Then they all trail down the road to eat. What a treat!

Maya may dream of ten eggs tonight.","cover_scene":"Ten brightly colored dinosaur eggs rolling down a winding road, a few cracking open with tiny dinosaurs peeking out."}
Noted.

{"title":"The Dino Boat Race","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur race","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Kiki and Miumiu made a boat race for the dinos.

Each dino got a small boat. Each boat had a bright sail.

"Stay on the trail!" said Kiki. "Do not float too far!"

T. rex let out a big roar. His boat took off fast.

Stegosaurus sat with his tail in the sea. His boat went slow.

Triceratops had a teal sail. She could reach the peak of the wave!

Then rain fell. The sea got mean. Waves hit each boat.

T. rex cried, "My boat has a leak!"

Brachiosaurus had a long neck. She could reach him. She lifted T. rex to her back.

They all sailed to the beach as a team.

No one came in last. Each dino got a treat.

"We can dream of the next race," said Miumiu.","cover_scene":"Colorful cartoon dinosaurs sailing small boats with bright sails across choppy blue waves toward a sandy beach."}

{"title":"The Big Dino Run","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur race","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya sees a new dino race. Sixty dinos will run!

Some dinos eat meat. Some eat leaves. Today they all race on one trail.

"Ready, set, go!" Maya cheers.

T. rex runs fast. His feet beat the dirt.

Raptor is quick and neat. He leaps each log.

Stegosaurus is slow. He stops to eat green leaves.

The trail goes up a steep peak. Rain makes the dirt slick.

Raptor slides! He lands in the mud with a splat.

T. rex stops. He waits. He helps Raptor stand.

Then both run. They reach the last gate at the same time!

The crowd claps. Two winners! Each gets a big green treat.

Maya grins. She likes a fast race. But she likes a good team more.","cover_scene":"A T. rex and a raptor racing side by side up a muddy hill trail with many other dinosaurs behind them."}

{"title":"Dino Camp by the Lake","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur camp","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"The dinos won the big race. Now they camp by the lake.

Raptor has a green tent. T. rex has a coat, but it is too tight!

They need a fire. Stegosaurus drags a big load of oak logs.

Triceratops sets out a meal. She has beans, peas, and a bowl of oats.

"Eat up!" she says. "We ran all day."

T. rex wants meat. He goes to the lake to fish.

Splash! He gets soaked. But he gets three fat fish, too.

They toast the fish and eat by the heat of the fire.

The moon goes up. An owl hoots.

Raptor tells a tale of a ghost dino that roams the road.

T. rex peeks out. He sees just a goat!

The dinos laugh and sleep. What a fine day.","cover_scene":"Cartoon dinosaurs sitting around a campfire beside a moonlit lake with tents and oak trees nearby."}

{"title":"The Fossil Dig","level":2,"topic":"fossil dig","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya goes to dino camp. Today the kids will dig for fossils!

The teacher gives each kid a pail and a small pick.

"Dig slow," she says. "A fossil can crack."

Maya kneels in the sand. She sweeps with her hand.

Tink! Her pick hits something hard.

She leans in close. She sees a gray shape in the clay.

"It is a tooth!" Maya cheers. "A real dino tooth!"

The teacher beams. "That tooth ate meat long ago."

Next the kids make a clay volcano. They pour in soap and it foams!

The goo creeps down like hot lava. The kids squeal.

At the end of the day, Maya takes her tooth home in a box.

She keeps it by her bed. Each night she dreams of dinos.","cover_scene":"A girl kneeling in a sandy dig pit with a brush, lifting a large fossil tooth from the ground while other kids dig nearby."}

{"title":"Maya at the Museum","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur museum","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya goes to the museum. Big bones stand in the main hall!

A tall skeleton greets her. It is a T. rex. Its teeth are as long as her hand.

"Scientists found each bone in the ground," says Dad. "Then they put them back in place."

Maya sees a plate from a Stegosaurus back. She sees a claw. She sees a nest of eggs in gray stone.

Then Maya plays a game on a screen. She must match eight fossils to the right dino.

Click! The tail goes to the raptor. Click! The beak goes to the Triceratops.

She gets them all. The screen cheers!

Last, Maya draws her own dino. She gives it green skin, a long neck, and a sail.

"I will name it Maya-saurus," she says.","cover_scene":"A girl looking up at a huge T. rex skeleton in a bright museum hall, with a drawing pad tucked under her arm."}

{"title":"Maya-saurus Wakes Up","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur dream","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"That night, Maya dreams her drawing is real.

Maya-saurus stands by her bed! She has green skin, a long neck, and a tall sail.

"Climb on," she says. "I will show you my home."

Maya holds the sail. They float out the window and soar.

They land in a green field. Ferns grow up to Maya's waist.

Maya-saurus eats leaves from a tall tree. She reaches the top with ease.

A stream runs near. They both drink. The water is cool and clean.

Then Maya sees a real T. rex! He lets out a deep roar.

"Do not fear," says Maya-saurus. "He just yawned!"

The T. rex naps in the heat. His teeth gleam in the sun.

Maya paints the scene in her mind. Then she wakes in her own bed and grins.","cover_scene":"A girl riding on the back of a friendly green sail-backed dinosaur soaring over a ferny prehistoric valley at dusk."}
Noted.

{"title":"Lilani and the Dino Cave","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur dreams","target_skill":"silent_e","text":"Lilani and her brother Eesa share one dream at night.

In the dream, they ride a kind dino down a stone lane.

They come to a wide cave. Inside, it is bright as day!

A baby dino is stuck by a huge rock. He makes a small whine.

"We can save him!" says Lilani.

Eesa takes a long pine pole. He uses it like a lever. The rock slides!

The baby is safe. He gives Lilani's hand a lick with his tongue.

His mom comes home. She is the size of a house! But she is not mean. She smiles.

She gives them a ride on her spine, back up the lane.

Then the dream fades. Lilani wakes. Eesa wakes.

"Same dream?" she asks.

"Same dream," he smiles.","cover_scene":"Two children riding on the back of a gentle dinosaur toward a glowing wide cave at night."}

{"title":"The Dino at the Aquarium","level":2,"topic":"aquarium dinosaur","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya goes to the aquarium. She sees a real octopus!

It has eight arms. It creeps on the glass and peeks at her.

"Long ago, sea reptiles ruled here," says the guide. "They were not dinosaurs, but they lived at the same time."

Maya sees a big bone shape on the wall. It has a long neck and flat feet like oars.

"That one ate fish," says the guide. "It could not walk on land. It swam."

Maya leans close to the tank. A ray floats by. Eels hide in the reef.

A seal claps its tail. The crowd cheers.

Maya eats a snack by the window. Boats sail past on the bay.

She dreams of a sea dino in that deep green water.

"I will read all about them," she says.","cover_scene":"A girl pressing her hands to a huge aquarium window where an octopus peeks back, with a long-necked sea reptile skeleton on the wall behind her."}

{"title":"The Giant with the Heavy Tail","level":2,"topic":"giant dinosaur","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya reads the dino news. A new giant was found!

Its name is Dreadnoughtus. It is one of the biggest dinos we know.

It was as long as a whole train. Its tail was so heavy!

Maya paints a picture of it. She uses green and brown paint.

In her mind she sees it. The giant walks by a stream. Its feet leave deep tracks in the clay.

It reaches up to eat leaves from the tallest tree. It eats all day. It needs a lot of food!

No beast can beat it. It is too big. It just roams the plain and eats.

Then rain falls. The giant drinks. It sleeps by the oak trees.

Maya hangs her painting by her bed.

"Sleep well, big one," she says. "See you in my dreams."","cover_scene":"An enormous long-necked dinosaur with a huge heavy tail walking beside a stream, dwarfing the trees around it."}

{"title":"The Octopus and the Dino Tracks","level":2,"topic":"octopus dinosaur","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Did you know an octopus has three hearts? Maya did!

She tells her class at school. "It has eight arms and blue blood, too."

Then her teacher shares big news. In the UK, people found dino footprints under tonnes of rock!

The prints are insanely big. One foot is wider than Maya!

A sauropod made them long ago. That beast was as long as five cars.

The class goes out to the sand pit. Each kid makes tracks.

Maya makes a deep round print with a pail. Then she makes a trail of them.

"Read my tracks," she says. "Which way did my dino go?"

Her friend Jean follows the trail to the oak tree.

"It went to eat leaves!" Jean cheers.

Maya beams. She wants to hunt real tracks one day.","cover_scene":"Kids in a sandy schoolyard making giant round dinosaur footprints, with a smiling octopus drawing on a poster behind them."}

{"title":"Deep Sea Monsters?","level":2,"topic":"octopus facts","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya reads about octopuses in the deep.

They have round bodies and big bulging eyes. Each one has eight long arms.

Octopuses live in each ocean. They like warm, sunny seas best.

Some people call them "monsters of the deep." But they are not mean at all.

Most stay near the ocean floor. They creep on the sand and peek in each hole.

An octopus can change its coat! It can turn gray like a stone or green like a weed. Then you cannot see it.

If a big fish comes, it shoots a cloud of ink and speeds away.

Its cousin is the squid. Both are clever.

Maya draws one on a sheet of paper. She gives it eight neat arms.

"Not a monster," she says. "Just a sea friend."","cover_scene":"A round-bodied octopus with big eyes and eight curling arms resting on a sandy ocean floor near green seaweed."}

{"title":"The Tide Pool Hunt","level":3,"topic":"tide pools","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya and her friend Jean explore the tide pools at dawn, when the sea creeps back and leaves shallow pools behind.

Each pool is a tiny ocean. Green weeds sway. Snails crawl. A crab waves one claw and scoots beneath a stone.

"Keep your hands out," says Jean. "Just look."

Maya leans close and sees a small octopus squeezed into a crack. Its round eyes gleam. It has eight arms, and each arm feels along the rock for a meal.

Then it turns pale gray, exactly like the stone. Maya blinks. It seems to have gone!

The girls stay until the sea sweeps back in and fills each pool again.

On the beach, Maya finds a spiral shell. She keeps it to remember the day she met a monster of the deep who was not a monster at all.","cover_scene":"Two girls crouching over a rocky tide pool at dawn, a small octopus tucked in a crevice among green seaweed and a crab."}

{"title":"Fifteen Things in a Tide Pool","level":3,"topic":"tide pools","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya keeps a green notebook. Today she will count fifteen things in one tide pool.

One: a sea star with five slow arms. Two: a snail that creeps up the steep rock wall. Three: a heap of green weeds that sway each time a wave sweeps in.

Four and five: two crabs that scoot beneath a stone.

Six: a tiny fish. Seven: a barnacle. When the tide reaches it, it opens and sweeps food into its mouth.

Maya keeps counting. Eight sea grapes. Nine bright shells. Ten little eels in a crack.

By fourteen, her feet are soaked and her cheeks feel the sea breeze.

Fifteen: her own face, floating on the still water, peeking back at her.

She writes the last line neatly. Then the tide creeps in and takes the whole pool away.","cover_scene":"A girl with a green notebook kneeling beside a rocky tide pool full of sea stars, crabs, snails and seaweed."}

{"title":"The Tide Pool Club","level":3,"topic":"tide pool club","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya and Jean started a club. They meet each Saturday at the beach at low tide.

Their rule is simple: look, learn, and leave everything where it lays.

Today three more kids joined. Maya teaches them what she knows.

"A tide pool is like a tiny ocean that the sea leaves behind," she explains. "Twice each day the water sweeps back in. The creatures here must survive both the deep water and the hot sun."

She points out a sea star creeping toward a mussel. She shows them how a crab breathes and how seaweed feels slick and cool.

"Never pry a snail off a rock," Jean adds. "It needs that grip to keep from drying out."

The kids kneel and peer for a whole hour. Nobody speaks much.

Then the tide reaches their feet, and the club cheers and races up the beach.","cover_scene":"Five kids kneeling in a row around a wide rocky tide pool at low tide, with the ocean behind them."}

{"title":"Louder Than Thunder","level":3,"topic":"rockets","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya learned a new fact: a rocket launch is louder than thunder.

She told her whole class about it at the morning meeting.

"When a rocket leaves the ground, it burns fuel so fast that the sound shakes the air for miles," she explained. "People stand far away and still feel it in their chests."

Her teacher smiled and streamed a real launch on the screen.

The crowd waited. Steam poured from the tail. Then the engines lit, bright as a small sun, and the rocket rose on a long white plume.

The roar reached them even through the speakers. Maya's ears rang.

"It sounds like the sea and thunder together," said Jean.

That night, Maya dreamed she was strapped in a seat, reading the countdown out loud.

Three. Two. One.

She leaned back and felt the whole world shake beneath her.","cover_scene":"A rocket lifting off on a bright plume of flame and steam while a girl watches from a field far below."}

{"title":"The Bubble-Powered Rocket","level":3,"topic":"rocket science","target_skill":"silent_e","text":"Maya found a NASA page for kids. It showed how to make a bubble-powered rocket at home.

She gathered the supplies: a paper tube, tape, a film case with a tight lid, and one fizzy tablet.

Jean came over to help. They made a cone for the nose and three fins for the side.

"Now the fun part," Maya said. She poured water inside the case, dropped in half a tablet, and pressed the lid on tight.

They set the rocket on the driveway and stepped back.

The tablet made gas. The gas had no place to escape. The pressure rose and rose.

POP! The lid blew off and the whole rocket shot five times higher than the gate.

Jean shouted. Maya smiled wide.

"Real rockets work the same way," she said. "Something pushes down, so the rocket rides up."

They made nine more launches before dinnertime.","cover_scene":"Two kids in a driveway watching a homemade paper rocket blast upward in a spray of fizzy water."}

{"title":"Maya Wants to Be an Astronaut","level":2,"topic":"astronaut","target_skill":"silent_e","text":"Maya wants to be an astronaut.

She makes a space suit from tape and a white bag. She makes a hat from a pail.

"Time to ride," she says.

Her bed is the space plane. Her lamp is the sun.

Maya sits inside. She takes the stick in her hand.

"Five, four, three, two, one!"

The plane shakes. Up she goes! She waves at home as it gets small.

In space she can float. She spins like a top. Her cup of juice floats, too!

She sees the whole globe. It is blue and white.

She finds a stone from the moon and puts it in a tube.

Then it is time to come home. She rides the flame back down.

Maya lands safe on her rug.

"Same time next week," she smiles.","cover_scene":"A girl in a homemade cardboard space suit floating above her bed with the blue Earth glowing outside her window."}

{"title":"Planets Like Cotton Candy","level":2,"topic":"space news","target_skill":"silent_e","text":"Maya reads a space page for kids.

It says there are "super-puff" planets far out in space.

These planets are huge. But they are not dense like stone. They are less dense than cotton candy!

Maya makes a face. "Can I take a bite?"

Dad smiles. "No. They are not made of candy. They are made of gas."

Maya thinks of a big pink cloud the size of a whole globe.

She grabs her white paper and makes five of them. She names them: Fluff, Puff, Cake, Lime, and Mike.

She tapes them up by her bed.

Then she reads one more line. Soon a huge space scope will fly up and look for more.

"I hope it finds ten!" says Maya.

She turns off her lamp. In her dream, she floats past each one.","cover_scene":"A girl in bed gazing at five fluffy pastel planets drawn on paper taped to her wall, with a telescope by the window."}

transcript.title: The Dino Team by the Sea
transcript.text:
Maya reads about dinosaurs each day. She reads facts and sees big art of them.

Today she reads about a dino team by the sea.

A green dino ate leaves. Her name was Bean. She had a long neck and a long tail.

A gray dino ate meat. His name was Coal. He could roar and leap!

Rain fell on the sea. Bean and Coal ran to a cave to stay dry.

"Wait!" said Bean. "A snail is in the rain!"

Coal made a road with a leaf. The snail sailed to the cave. Safe!

The rain went away. The sun came up. Bean ate leaves. Coal took a nap in the heat.

Maya read the last page. She can see the dino team in her mind: Bean, Coal, and the snail on the leaf.

Maya will read more facts each day. Dinosaurs are the best!

chapters.title: The Dino Trail
chapters.text:
Maya and Dad take a trail to the museum. The sign reads: MEET THE DINOSAURS!

A big beast stands in the hall. Its teeth are as long as Maya's arm. Its tail is like a road.

"That is a meat eater," Dad says.

Maya reads the sign. She says each word slow. Ea says /ee/. Ai says /ay/. Oa says /oh/.

She sees a dino with a beak. She sees a dino with a green coat of scales. She sees eggs in a nest of leaves.

A man in a lab coat waits by the last case. "Want to hold a real claw?" he asks.

Maya nods. The claw feels cold. It feels heavy. Her cheeks glow.

At home, Maya paints a dino on a sheet. She gives it a long tail and a wide beak.

"I will be a dino hunter," she says. "I will dig and read and learn."

transcript.title: Dino Eggs in the Oak Woods
transcript.text:
Maya loves dinosaur news. Today she reads about eggs.

Long ago, a dino made a nest by an oak tree. She laid three eggs in the soft dirt.

The mom was named Oat. She had a big beak and a long tail.

Oat ate green leaves all day. She did not leave the nest.

Rain came. Oat kept the eggs dry. Heat came. Oat made shade with a leaf.

One day a crack! A peep! A tiny dino came out of the egg.

Then two more! Three baby dinos, each with a tiny beak.

Oat let them eat seeds and leaves. They ate a lot!

The babies did not stray far. They kept close to Oat by the oak.

Maya read the page again. Scientists find real dino eggs in rock! Maya wants to find one, too.

chapters.title: Dino Rain Day
chapters.text:
Rain fell on the green hills. A big dino ate leaves by the lake.

Her name was Oak. Oak had a long neck and a flat beak.

The rain made a stream. The stream ran fast. Oak let out a squeak!

A small dino sat on a boat of bark. He float, float, floated!

"Wait!" said Oak. "I will help. Take my tail!"

The small dino did not wait. He grabbed the tail and held on.

Oak did not drop him. She made a road with her neck. Step, step, step!

Soon both dinos sat on dry soil. They ate leaves and beans in the heat.

The rain went away. A bright sun came out.

Real kids read about dinos each day. Scientists dig and find new bones! Some dinos had a beak. Some had a coat of feathers.

Oak did not read. Oak just ate leaves.

But Oak was a real, brave dino.

transcript.title: Ten Surprise Eggs
transcript.text:
Maya sees a fun show. Ten eggs roll down a road!

Each egg has a coat of paint.

The teal egg cracks. Out leaps a T. rex! He lets out a loud roar.

The gray egg cracks. Out peeks a Brachiosaurus. Her neck is so tall she can reach the leaves.

The green egg cracks. A Velociraptor! She is fast on the trail.

The red egg cracks. A Stegosaurus. He eats weeds all day.

The blue egg cracks. A Triceratops. She has three horns.

The last egg cracks. An Ankylosaurus! His tail is like a big oak club.

Maya claps. "Wait! I must count them!"

She counts each one. Ten dinos in a neat row.

Then they all trail down the road to eat. What a treat!

Maya may dream of ten eggs tonight.

chapters.title: The Dino Boat Team
chapters.text:
Sam has a boat. The boat is on the lake.

Three toy dinos sit in the boat. They are a team.

The big one has a green coat of paint. He can float!

The small one has a beak. It can eat leaves.

The last one has a long tail.

Sam reads a book about dinos. The book says real dinos did not sail. But they did wade! They did eat!

Rain! Big drops hit the lake. The boat rocks.

"Wait!" says Sam. "Hold on, team!"

The dino with the tail tips out. Splash! He floats away.

Sam takes a deep breath. He reaches out. He gets the dino!

The rain stops. The lake is calm.

Sam sets the boat on the road home. His team is safe.

"Good team," says Sam. "Next week we sail again."

The dinos do not speak. But Sam thinks they are glad.

transcript.title: The Dino Boat Race
transcript.text:
Kiki and Miumiu made a boat race for the dinos.

Each dino got a small boat. Each boat had a bright sail.

"Stay on the trail!" said Kiki. "Do not float too far!"

T. rex let out a big roar. His boat took off fast.

Stegosaurus sat with his tail in the sea. His boat went slow.

Triceratops had a teal sail. She could reach the peak of the wave!

Then rain fell. The sea got mean. Waves hit each boat.

T. rex cried, "My boat has a leak!"

Brachiosaurus had a long neck. She could reach him. She lifted T. rex to her back.

They all sailed to the beach as a team.

No one came in last. Each dino got a treat.

"We can dream of the next race," said Miumiu.

chapters.title: Dino Seed Snack
chapters.text:
Little Dino had a beak. His beak was made to eat.

Today the team had a plan. They would eat a big meal by the road.

Rain fell on the trail. Drip, drip, drip! But the team did not wait.

Dino saw a seed on a leaf. He ate the seed with his beak. Yum!

His pal Sail had a long tail. Her tail made a path in the rain.

The team ran to a boat. The boat sat on a lake. Hop, hop! All aboard!

The boat did float. It did not sink. Dino ate a green leaf on the boat.

The rain went away. The sun came out. Dino gave a happy squeak.

Scientists still dig up dino bones today. They read the bones like a book. Each bone can teach us a new fact!

Dino ate the last seed. "That was a fine meal," said the team.

transcript.title: The Big Dino Run
transcript.text:
Maya sees a new dino race. Sixty dinos will run!

Some dinos eat meat. Some eat leaves. Today they all race on one trail.

"Ready, set, go!" Maya cheers.

T. rex runs fast. His feet beat the dirt.

Raptor is quick and neat. He leaps each log.

Stegosaurus is slow. He stops to eat green leaves.

The trail goes up a steep peak. Rain makes the dirt slick.

Raptor slides! He lands in the mud with a splat.

T. rex stops. He waits. He helps Raptor stand.

Then both run. They reach the last gate at the same time!

The crowd claps. Two winners! Each gets a big green treat.

Maya grins. She likes a fast race. But she likes a good team more.

chapters.title: Dino Trail and the Green Coast
chapters.text:
Rain fell on the green trail. A big dino woke up.

"I will find my team," she said.

She made a wide trail in the mud. Her tail left a deep mark. Snails sat on a leaf.

Soon she saw the coast. A boat did float near the road. A small dino sat in it and ate a meal.

"Come eat!" he said. "I have leaves and seeds."

The big dino ate. The rain did stop. A sail went up, white and neat.

They did float down the coast. A bird with a long beak came too. It sat on the mast to nap.

"We are a team," said the big dino. "I can teach you the trail. You can teach me the sea."

They rode home at sunset.

Real dino fans read facts and play games at Nat Geo Kids. New science teaches us more each year!

transcript.text:
The dinos won the big race. Now they camp by the lake.

Raptor has a green tent. T. rex has a coat, but it is too tight!

They toast the fish and eat by the heat of the fire.

The moon goes up. An owl hoots.

Raptor tells a tale of a ghost dino that roams the road.

T. rex peeks out. He sees just a goat!

chapters.title: Dino Rain on the Oak Road
chapters.text:
Rain fell on the oak road. A big dino team came out to play.

"Rain, rain!" said Pip. "I like rain!"

Pip led the team down the trail. The trail was wet. Each foot made a deep track in the mud.

A green leaf fell. Pip ate the leaf. It was a good meal!

The trail met the coast. A boat sat on the sand. The boat had a big sail.

"Can we sail?" said Pip.

"We can sail!" said the team.

The team got in the boat. The sail went up. Rain fell on the sail. The boat went down the coast.

Pip ate one more leaf on the way.

At home, Pip read a book. Real people dig up dino bones each year. They teach us what each dino ate!

"I like that," said Pip. "I ate a leaf too."

Rain fell on the oak road all night.

transcript.title: The Fossil Dig
transcript.text:
Maya goes to dino camp. Today the kids will dig for fossils!

The teacher gives each kid a pail and a small pick.

"Dig slow," she says. "A fossil can crack."

Maya kneels in the sand. She sweeps with her hand.

Tink! Her pick hits something hard.

She leans in close. She sees a gray shape in the clay.

"It is a tooth!" Maya cheers. "A real dino tooth!"

The teacher beams. "That tooth ate meat long ago."

Next the kids make a clay volcano. They pour in soap and it foams!

The goo creeps down like hot lava. The kids squeal.

At the end of the day, Maya takes her tooth home in a box.

She keeps it by her bed. Each night she dreams of dinos.

chapters.title: The Dino Boat Race
chapters.text:
Rex and Pip are a team. A dino team!

Today the team will sail a boat. The boat sits by the coast. The sea is calm. No rain. Not one drop of rain.

"Each of us can sail," says Rex. "I will teach you."

Pip gets a big green leaf. The leaf is her sail! Rex takes the oars. The team sails the boat away from the coast.

Soon, rain! Rain taps the boat. Rain taps the leaf. Pip holds the sail tight.

"Keep on!" says Rex. "We sail as a team!"

The rain stops. The boat lands on a sand trail. The trail goes up the road to home.

On the road, the team eats a meal. Each dino eats a leaf. Each dino is glad.

Did you know? Kids can read real dino facts and see dino art on the web. You can read and learn each day, just like Pip!

Maya goes to the museum. Big bones stand in the main hall!

A tall skeleton greets her. It is a T. rex. Its teeth are as long as her hand.

"Scientists found each bone in the ground," says Dad. "Then they put them back in place."

Maya sees a plate from a Stegosaurus back. She sees a claw. She sees a nest of eggs in gray stone.

Then Maya plays a game on a screen. She must match eight fossils to the right dino.

Click! The tail goes to the raptor. Click! The beak goes to the Triceratops.

She gets them all. The screen cheers!

Last, Maya draws her own dino. She gives it green skin, a long neck, and a sail.

"I will name it Maya-saurus," she says.

chapters.title: Stomp and the Shiny Shell
chapters.text:
Stomp is a big dino. Stomp has strong legs.

Stomp went down the steep path. Crunch! Crack! Stomp stepped on twigs.

Stomp saw a shiny shell in the sand. The shell was flat and smooth.

"Whose shell is this?" said Stomp.

A small dino ran up fast. "That is my shell!" she said. "I am Skip."

Skip and Stomp sat by the stream. They shared plums and green leaves.

Splash! A fish did a flip. Skip and Stomp did a flip too. Stomp fell flat, and Skip did a big grin.

Then Skip held up the shell. "You can keep it," said Skip. "A gift for a friend."

Stomp held the shell close. It shone like a star.

At home, Stomp read a dino book from Nat Geo Kids. It had facts, games, and art. Stomp read that new dino facts come out each year!

"Dinos are the best," said Stomp.

transcript.title: Maya-saurus Wakes Up
transcript.text:
That night, Maya dreams her drawing is real.

Maya-saurus stands by her bed! She has green skin, a long neck, and a tall sail.

"Climb on," she says. "I will show you my home."

Maya holds the sail. They float out the window and soar.

They land in a green field. Ferns grow up to Maya's waist.

Maya-saurus eats leaves from a tall tree. She reaches the top with ease.

A stream runs near. They both drink. The water is cool and clean.

Then Maya sees a real T. rex! He lets out a deep roar.

"Do not fear," says Maya-saurus. "He just yawned!"

The T. rex naps in the heat. His teeth gleam in the sun.

Maya paints the scene in her mind. Then she wakes in her own bed and grins.

chapters.title: Chip the Dino Chef
chapters.text:
Chip was a dino chef. Chip had a big chef hat and a shiny dish.

"What shall I make?" said Chip. "I wish to make lunch for the whole pack!"

Chip put fresh fish in the dish. Chip put thick chunks of squash in the dish. Chip put chips on the shelf.

Whoosh! The wind shook the shed. Crash! The dish shook too.

"Which way did my lunch go?" said Chip.

Chip shut the shed. Chip checked the shelf. Chip checked the chest. Then Chip checked the path.

There! Three dino chicks had the fish. They had the squash. They had the chips!

The chicks did not munch. They did not chomp. They shared with Chip!

"Thanks, chicks," said Chip. "This is the best lunch. Munch, crunch, chomp!"

Did you wish for more dino facts? Kids can check National Geographic Kids. It has dino facts, dino art, and dino games. Such fun!

transcript.title: Lilani and the Dino Cave
transcript.text:
Lilani and her brother Eesa share one dream at night.

In the dream, they ride a kind dino down a stone lane.

They come to a wide cave. Inside, it is bright as day!

A baby dino is stuck by a huge rock. He makes a small whine.

"We can save him!" says Lilani.

Eesa takes a long pine pole. He uses it like a lever. The rock slides!

The baby is safe. He gives Lilani's hand a lick with his tongue.

His mom comes home. She is the size of a house! But she is not mean. She smiles.

She gives them a ride on her spine, back up the lane.

Then the dream fades. Lilani wakes. Eesa wakes.

"Same dream?" she asks.

"Same dream," he smiles.

chapters.title: Chomp Finds a Chunk
chapters.text:
Chomp was a small dino. Chomp liked to munch.

Chomp ran to the branch. On the branch was a bunch of red fruit.

"I wish I could reach!" said Chomp.

Chomp gave the branch a push. A chunk of fruit fell. Chomp did a little chomp. Crunch! Munch!

Then Chomp chose one more chunk. Crunch, crunch, munch!

A chick ran up. The chick did not have lunch.

"Do you wish for a chunk?" said Chomp.

The chick gave a chirp. Chomp put a chunk in a dish. The chick ate the chunk in the dish. Crunch!

Chomp and the chick sat on the branch. They ate lunch. Munch, munch, crunch!

Some kids read facts about dinos like Chomp. Chomp is a hit!

Chomp gave a big chomp and did not wish for one more thing.

transcript.text:
Maya goes to the aquarium. She sees a real octopus!

It has eight arms. It creeps on the glass and peeks at her.

"Long ago, sea reptiles ruled here," says the guide. "They were not dinosaurs, but they lived at the same time."

Maya sees a big bone shape on the wall. It has a long neck and flat feet like oars.

"That one ate fish," says the guide. "It could not walk on land. It swam."

Maya leans close to the tank. A ray floats by. Eels hide in the reef.

A seal claps its tail. The crowd cheers.

Maya eats a snack by the window. Boats sail past on the bay.

She dreams of a sea dino in that deep green water.

"I will read all about them," she says.

chapters.title: Chet the Deep-Sea Fish
chapters.text:
Chet is a small fish. Chet lives deep, deep down in the sea.

It is dark down there. No sun. Just cold water and soft mud.

One day, a ship sent down a light. Swish! Chet swam past it. Swish! Chet swam past it again.

The light was a camera. Up on the ship, a team of scientists sat and watched.

"Look!" said one. "A new fish! No one has seen this fish!"

They did not wish for a big, scary beast. They got Chet. Chet is pink. Chet is soft. Chet has a chin like a chip.

"He is adorable," said the scientist. That made her grin.

Chet did a flip. Splash! Swish! He did not chomp. He did not dash.

Chet is a snailfish. He lives two miles down. Now we can wish him well.

Swish, swish, Chet. Swim home.

"Chan, Chet, I will show you my home," it said.

So Chan and Chet and the pink fish went on a dash in the deep.

transcript.title: The Octopus and the Dino Tracks
transcript.text:
Did you know an octopus has three hearts? Maya did!

She tells her class at school. "It has eight arms and blue blood, too."

Then her teacher shares big news. In the UK, people found dino footprints under tonnes of rock!

The prints are insanely big. One foot is wider than Maya!

A sauropod made them long ago. That beast was as long as five cars.

The class goes out to the sand pit. Each kid makes tracks.

Maya makes a deep round print with a pail. Then she makes a trail of them.

"Read my tracks," she says. "Which way did my dino go?"

Her friend Jean follows the trail to the oak tree.

"It went to eat leaves!" Jean cheers.

Maya beams. She wants to hunt real tracks one day.

chapters.title: Chip the Shy Octopus
chapters.text:
Chip is a shy octopus. Chip hides in a dish-shaped shell.

A fish swims past. Swish! Chip hides. Chip does not wish to be seen.

Then Chip sees a chest in the sand. Chip chose to peek. Chip lifts the lid with one arm. Splash!

In the chest is a small, soft snailfish. It came from way, way down deep. Scientists found one like it, miles below the waves. They said it was cute, not scary!

"Can we be chums?" asks Chip.

"Yes!" says the snailfish. "I wish for a chum."

Chip gives the snailfish a chunk of crab shell to hide in. The snailfish gives Chip a shiny shell chip.

They chase. They dash. They splash.

Now Chip is not shy. Chip has a chum, and the fish has a chum too.

Swish, swish! Off they dash to the deep.

transcript.title: Deep Sea Monsters?
transcript.text:
Maya reads about octopuses in the deep.

They have round bodies and big bulging eyes. Each one has eight long arms.

Octopuses live in each ocean. They like warm, sunny seas best.

Some people call them "monsters of the deep." But they are not mean at all.

Most stay near the ocean floor. They creep on the sand and peek in each hole.

An octopus can change its coat! It can turn gray like a stone or green like a weed. Then you cannot see it.

If a big fish comes, it shoots a cloud of ink and speeds away.

Its cousin is the squid. Both are clever.

Maya draws one on a sheet of paper. She gives it eight neat arms.

"Not a monster," she says. "Just a sea friend."

chapters.title: Nell the Sea Turtle Meets the Deep Team
chapters.text:
Nell is a sea turtle with green feet. She likes to sleep in the weeds near the reef.

One day a boat sailed by. A team of scientists sat on the deck. They had a deep-sea robot with a bright beam.

"Wait for me!" said Nell. She swam past the boat to peek.

The robot sank down, down, down. It went two miles below the waves. That is deeper than deep!

The beam lit up a tiny fish. It was pink and neat, with a small sweet face. No one had seen this fish before. It was a new kind of snailfish!

"It is not big. It is not mean," said a scientist. "It is adorable!"

Nell could not reach that deep. But she could dream. She thought of the tiny pink fish in the dark, sweet and free.

Nell swam back to her weeds to sleep. She had a fine dream about the deep.

transcript.title: The Tide Pool Hunt
transcript.text:
Maya and her friend Jean explore the tide pools at dawn, when the sea creeps back and leaves shallow pools behind.

Each pool is a tiny ocean. Green weeds sway. Snails crawl. A crab waves one claw and scoots beneath a stone.

"Keep your hands out," says Jean. "Just look."

Maya leans close and sees a small octopus squeezed into a crack. Its round eyes gleam. It has eight arms, and each arm feels along the rock for a meal.

Then it turns pale gray, exactly like the stone. Maya blinks. It seems to have gone!

The girls stay until the sea sweeps back in and fills each pool again.

On the beach, Maya finds a spiral shell. She keeps it to remember the day she met a monster of the deep who was not a monster at all.

chapters.title: Bree and the Great Grass Reef
chapters.text:
Bree was a small brown crab who lived by a great green reef. Every morning she swam out to the grass beds to trade shells with her friends.

One day a strong current swept a bright blue trap onto the reef. Bree swam close. Inside the trap, a tiny snailfish was trying to get free.

"Grab my claw!" Bree said. But the trap was strong.

So Bree called her brave friends. A swordfish swam up. Two gray shrimp came too. Together they pulled and pressed until the trap broke, and the snailfish swam free.

"Scientists just found a snailfish like me," it said, "more than two miles down in the deep Pacific. They said we were adorable!"

Bree grinned. "You are! Grand and brave, too."

The snailfish swam a slow loop around the green grass, and every crab on the great reef cheered.

transcript.title: Fifteen Things in a Tide Pool
transcript.text:
Maya keeps a green notebook. Today she will count fifteen things in one tide pool.

One: a sea star with five slow arms. Two: a snail that creeps up the steep rock wall. Three: a heap of green weeds that sway each time a wave sweeps in.

Four and five: two crabs that scoot beneath a stone.

Six: a tiny fish. Seven: a barnacle. When the tide reaches it, it opens and sweeps food into its mouth.

Maya keeps counting. Eight sea grapes. Nine bright shells. Ten little eels in a crack.

By fourteen, her feet are soaked and her cheeks feel the sea breeze.

Fifteen: her own face, floating on the still water, peeking back at her.

She writes the last line neatly. Then the tide creeps in and takes the whole pool away.

chapters.title: Crab Trick and the Tiny Snailfish
chapters.text:
Crab lived by a crack in the bright reef. He liked to brag. "I am brave! I am grand!" he said.

One day a truck-shaped sub swam down from a boat. Real scientists were inside it. They were from a big aquarium, and they went down, down, down, more than two miles!

Crab crept close and swam behind the sub. "I will be brave too," he said.

Down in the cold dark, the crew found a small pink fish. It was a snailfish. No one had ever seen this kind before. It was not scary. It was tiny and sweet.

"Adorable!" one scientist cried.

Crab grinned. The snailfish did a slow, free swirl. Crab tried a swirl too, but he spun and bumped a grape-sized crumb of stone.

The crew swam up. Crab crept back to his crack.

"Brave crabs," he said, "and brave tiny fish. Both are grand."

transcript.title: The Tide Pool Club
transcript.text:
Maya and Jean started a club. They meet each Saturday at the beach at low tide.

Their rule is simple: look, learn, and leave everything where it lays.

Today three more kids joined. Maya teaches them what she knows.

"A tide pool is like a tiny ocean that the sea leaves behind," she explains. "Twice each day the water sweeps back in. The creatures here must survive both the deep water and the hot sun."

She points out a sea star creeping toward a mussel. She shows them how a crab breathes and how seaweed feels slick and cool.

"Never pry a snail off a rock," Jean adds. "It needs that grip to keep from drying out."

The kids kneel and peer for a whole hour. Nobody speaks much.

Then the tide reaches their feet, and the club cheers and races up the beach.

chapters.title: Trina and the Swift Green Submarine
chapters.text:
Trina was a scientist who loved the deep, dark sea. One gray morning she climbed into a swift green submarine and dropped down past the bright reef.

Down, down, down. Crabs crept over gray stones. A school of small fish swam by in a swirl of silver. Trina grinned and grabbed her notebook.

"Two miles down," she said. "Nobody has seen this spot before."

Her crew waited up on the boat. "Trust the lights," they said on the radio. "Tell us what you spot."

Then Trina saw it. A tiny snailfish, soft and pink, drifting like a slow balloon. It was a brand new kind of fish, never seen by people.

"It is not scary at all," Trina said. "It is adorable!"

She swept the light across the dark. The snailfish swam a slow circle, then swam away.

Trina grinned all the way up. Her crew cheered. Science is grand.

transcript.title: Louder Than Thunder
transcript.text:
Maya learned a new fact: a rocket launch is louder than thunder.

She told her whole class about it at the morning meeting.

"When a rocket leaves the ground, it burns fuel so fast that the sound shakes the air for miles," she explained. "People stand far away and still feel it in their chests."

Her teacher smiled and streamed a real launch on the screen.

The crowd waited. Steam poured from the tail. Then the engines lit, bright as a small sun, and the rocket rose on a long white plume.

The roar reached them even through the speakers. Maya's ears rang.

"It sounds like the sea and thunder together," said Jean.

That night, Maya dreamed she was strapped in a seat, reading the countdown out loud.

Three. Two. One.

She leaned back and felt the whole world shake beneath her.

chapters.title: Nadia and the Bubble-Powered Rocket
chapters.text:
Nadia wanted to be a scientist, so she built a bubble-powered rocket from a plastic tube and a bright paper cone.

Her brother Grant brought the fizzy tablet. "Stand back," Nadia said. "This rocket may be small, but it will still make a splash."

She dropped the tablet in, snapped the cap tight, and set the rocket on the flat stone launch pad. Bubbles swirled and crowded inside. Then... SPLAT! POP! The rocket sprang up, spun, and landed in the grass.

"Three feet!" Grant cheered.

Nadia scribbled in her notebook like a true scientist. She tried less water. She tried more. On the last try, the rocket sprang past the fence.

On a NASA page for kids, Nadia had read that real rockets blast up with the same trick: press stuff down, and it pushes back.

"Real rockets are louder than thunder," Nadia grinned. "But mine is louder than Grant!"

transcript.title: The Bubble-Powered Rocket
transcript.text:
Maya found a NASA page for kids. It showed how to make a bubble-powered rocket at home.

She gathered the supplies: a paper tube, tape, a film case with a tight lid, and one fizzy tablet.

Jean came over to help. They made a cone for the nose and three fins for the side.

"Now the fun part," Maya said. She poured water inside the case, dropped in half a tablet, and pressed the lid on tight.

They set the rocket on the driveway and stepped back.

The tablet made gas. The gas had no place to escape. The pressure rose and rose.

POP! The lid blew off and the whole rocket shot five times higher than the gate.

Jean shouted. Maya smiled wide.

"Real rockets work the same way," she said. "Something pushes down, so the rocket rides up."

They made nine more launches before dinnertime.

chapters.title: Maya and the Mars Notebook
chapters.text:
Maya kept a red notebook just for space. Inside it, she wrote every fact she learned from videos about rockets, the Moon, and Mars.

"A scientist writes things down," she said. "So I will too."

On Monday, Maya watched a rover roll across Mars. The rover had six strong wheels and a camera on a long arm. It crept over rust-colored stones, hunting for signs of ancient water.

Maya sketched the rover in her notebook. She labeled the wheels, the camera, and the little dish that beams messages home.

"How long does a message take?" she asked her dad.

"Many minutes," he said. "Mars is very far away."

Maya grinned and wrote that down too. Then she drew herself in a white spacesuit, standing beside the rover, waving at the camera.

Under the drawing she printed one brave sentence: Someday I will go and see Mars myself.

chapters.title: Maya and the White Space Station
chapters.text:
Maya put on her white spacesuit and stepped inside the tall rocket. She felt brave, even when the engines began to shake.

"Three, two, one!" said the crew. Flames made a bright line in the sky, and the rocket rose into space.

Soon Maya could see the space station shine like a huge kite made of glass and metal. Her ship came close. It docked with a gentle bump.

Inside, nothing stayed in place. Maya's pen drifted past her nose. A plate of food floated by like a slow balloon. She had to take hold of a rope to move.

Maya looked out the wide window at the blue Earth below. She made a note: "Space is quiet, and it is home for a while."

On NASA's kid pages, you can build a bubble-powered rocket and watch it rise. Maya smiled. Brave astronauts all start with one small launch.

transcript.title: Planets Like Cotton Candy
transcript.text:
Maya reads a space page for kids.

It says there are "super-puff" planets far out in space.

These planets are huge. But they are not dense like stone. They are less dense than cotton candy!

Maya makes a face. "Can I take a bite?"

Dad smiles. "No. They are not made of candy. They are made of gas."

Maya thinks of a big pink cloud the size of a whole globe.

She grabs her white paper and makes five of them. She names them: Fluff, Puff, Cake, Lime, and Mike.

She tapes them up by her bed.

Then she reads one more line. Soon a huge space scope will fly up and look for more.

"I hope it finds ten!" says Maya.

She turns off her lamp. In her dream, she floats past each one.

chapters.title: Maya and the Moon Base Lights
chapters.text:
Maya woke up inside the moon base at nine o'clock. The white walls seemed to shine, and the huge dome let the stars come close.

"Time to work," she said. "I like this job."

Maya took her space suit off its hook. She zipped it up and made sure the hose was tight. Then she stepped outside onto the fine gray dust.

Her job was to place five solar plates in a line. The plates would take light from the sun and make power for the base. Maya set each one in its frame, then closed the last clamp.

Soon every lamp in the dome began to glow. The whole base looked like a bright white stone on the moon.

Back home on Earth, NASA kids were building bubble-powered rockets to see how high they could fly. Maya smiled. "Maybe one of them will drive the next ship here," she said.

transcript.title: The Red Moon Night
transcript.text:
Maya reads a space note. Tonight the moon will glow red!

"It is a lunar eclipse," says Dad. "Earth slides in line with the sun and the moon."

Maya makes a plan. She takes a cake for a snack. She takes a blanket and a big cup of juice.

At nine, they go outside. The air is cold. Dad makes a fire in the stone pit.

The moon is white. It is the size of a dime in the sky.

Maya waits. She takes a bite of cake. She waits some more.

Then a dark shape creeps on the moon. Bit by bit, it hides the white.

Soon the whole moon is a deep red. It is like a rose!

"Wow," Maya says. "I hope I can see this same thing one more time."

"You will," says Dad. "In time."

chapters.title: Maya and the Bubble Rocket Race
chapters.text:
Maya woke up before the sun and made a plan. Today was the day of the bubble rocket race.

NASA Space Place says kids can build a bubble-powered rocket at home, and Maya wanted hers to take first place. She used a tube, some tape, and one fizzy tablet. The fizz made gas, and the gas made the rocket rise.

"Come here and stand behind this line," Maya told her whole class. "It is time!"

She set the rocket on its base, gave it a shake, and stepped back. Pop! The tube rose in a fine white line, up above the pine tree, and came down on the grass.

Everyone smiled. Maya wrote the time in her notebook.

"Real rockets take the same kind of push," she said. "Gas goes down, and the rocket goes up. Next time, we go higher!"

transcript.title: Why the Moon Turns Red
transcript.text:
Maya still thinks about the red moon.

"Why did it change?" she asks at school.

Her teacher smiles. "Let me show you. Come up here."

Maya holds a white globe. That is the moon. Jean holds a lamp. That is the sun. The teacher holds a blue ball. That is Earth.

Jean turns on the lamp. The teacher slides Earth in line, right between them.

Earth makes a big shade. The globe hides inside it.

"Now, why not black?" the teacher asks. "Why red?"

No one knows.

"Sunlight bends as it goes past Earth. Blue light gets lost. Red light does not. That red light lands on the moon."

Maya likes this. Every sunrise and sunset on Earth, all at once, shines on that stone.

She takes a note home. She tapes it by her bed with her planets.

chapters.title: Maya and the Spinning Launch Pad
chapters.text:
Maya woke up early, because today was the day of the big launch. She had a plan, and her plan was a fine one.

On the NASA kids page, Maya had read about launching a rocket from a spinning launch pad. Some rockets go up from a flat spot, but this one would spin first, like a stone on a rope, and then race above the clouds.

Maya made her rocket from a tube and tape. She wrote her name on the side in white. Then she set it in place on the spinning base.

"Three, two, one," she said. The pad spun. The rocket rose.

It went high above the pine trees, and for one whole moment it looked like a real star.

Maya smiled. Same time tomorrow, she thought. Next time, she would make it go higher.

transcript.title: Grandpa and the Bone Hall
transcript.text:
Grandpa takes Maya to the museum again.

They go to the bone hall. A huge spine hangs from the roof. It is a whale? No! It is a dino.

"Each bone was stone once," says Grandpa. "It takes a long, long time."

Maya likes the T. rex best. Its teeth are the size of her shoe.

Grandpa likes the small ones. He points at a dino with fine bones like a bird.

"This one had scales and wings," he says.

They make a game. Grandpa names a dino. Maya finds it on the case.

She wins five times! He wins three.

Then they take a break. They share a lime ice and sit by the wide glass.

"Same time next month?" asks Maya.

Grandpa smiles. "I hope so. You can be my guide."

chapters.title: Maya and the Great Sea Dragon Bones
chapters.text:
Maya and Grandpa reached the museum just as the doors opened. A team of scientists had cleaned a new giant, and today each guest could see it.

"Meet the sea dragon," said the guide. "It swam in a real ocean long ago, near the coast, and it ate fish all day."

Maya read the sign out loud. The bones were pale gray, and each tooth looked like a nail. The tail was so long it reached the far wall.

"Did it float?" Maya asked.

"It did," the guide said. "It had to lift its head to breathe air, just like a seal."

Grandpa sat on a seat while Maya made a neat sketch on a sheet of paper. She drew the beast, the waves, and a boat far away.

At home she read more facts online. Scientists still find new dinosaurs each year.

"Next time," Maya said, "I will read every sign."

transcript.title: Maya Builds a Skeleton
transcript.text:
On the museum website, Maya found a game where you rebuild a fossil skeleton.

The screen showed a heap of bones, all jumbled. Her job was to place each one where it belonged.

She dragged the skull to the top. Easy. Then came the neck bones, each one a little smaller than the last.

The ribs were harder. She kept sliding them to the wrong spot, and the screen beeped at her.

"Take your time," said Grandpa. "Real scientists spend years on this. Sometimes they only find a few pieces and must guess the rest."

Maya leaned closer. She lined up the long leg bones, then the great sweeping tail.

The last piece clicked into place.

The screen read: STEGOSAURUS. Plates along the spine. Ate leaves and ferns.

Maya beamed. "I knew it was a leaf eater," she said. "Look at those teeth."

chapters.title: Maya and the Dinosaur Footprint Trail
chapters.text:
Maya read a fact this year: scientists still find new dinosaur tracks each season. So she and Dad drove out to the creek to see a real trail.

The rain had stopped, and the air felt clean. Maya took a deep breath and leaned near the mud. There it was! A huge footprint, deep as a bowl, with three toes spread wide.

"That beast had a heavy tail," Dad said. "See how the tail left a groan-deep streak in the clay?"

Maya kneeled and placed her hand inside the print. Her whole hand fit near the heel. She could almost hear the creature breathe, almost see it drink at the stream while leaves floated by.

A team from the museum came to make a coat of plaster. It would dry, float free, and go on display.

"Read the sign each year," the leader said, "and you may read your own name on it."

transcript.title: The Fossil Word Hunt
transcript.text:
Grandpa printed a fossil puzzle page for Maya.

It was a word hunt. Twelve fossil words were hidden in a grid of letters, and she had to find each one.

She started with the easy ones. ROCK. BONE. TOOTH.

Then the harder ones appeared. LAYER. She traced it going down, one letter at a time.

"Layers matter," said Grandpa. "Mud and sand pile up on a dead creature, year after year. The deeper the layer, the older the fossil."

Maya circled SPECIMEN next. That means one thing a scientist keeps and studies.

She found CLAW and TEETH and SEAM and PEAT.

The last word took her ages. She nearly gave up. Then she saw it, reading backward along the bottom row: REMAINS.

Twelve out of twelve.

"Same puzzle tomorrow?" she asked.

"There are eighteen more pages," Grandpa said.

"Scientists learn new dinosaur facts each year," Dad said. "You can read them, see art, and play games too."

Maya beamed. She would lead her own dig team someday, and each day she would teach the world one neat new thing.

transcript.title: Fossil Words
transcript.text:
Grandpa told Maya about a strange kind of fossil.

"Not a bone," he said. "A word."

A fossil word is one you almost never hear by itself anymore. It only appears inside a certain phrase, like a tiny piece of something old, stuck in the language.

"Give me one," Maya said.

"Fro. As in, to and fro. Nobody says fro alone."

Maya laughed. She started a list in her green notebook.

Kith, from kith and kin. Shrift, from short shrift. Dint, from by dint of.

"They got sealed in, like a leaf in stone," she said.

"Exactly. The rest of the sentence keeps them safe. Without it, they would have disappeared years ago."

Maya read her list again, slowly. Each word was old, and still breathing.

"So I am a paleontologist either way," she said. "Bones or words."

Maya leaned over a heavy bone. "Fact one: this beast had a tail as long as a bus!"

The old floor gave a low groan as she climbed the step. Maya reached the top shelf and found a fossil egg in a soft coat of sand.

"Fact three," she said, "babies hatched from eggs like this one!"

Dr. Reed beamed. "Each fact is true. You did not cheat, and you did not guess. You read."

transcript.title: The Science Journal
transcript.text:
Maya's teacher handed out a real science article, rewritten for kids.

It was about a team of paleontologists working in a dry streambed. For three seasons they found nothing but plain gray stone.

Then, in the fourth season, an intern noticed a strange gleam in a broken piece. Inside were teeth. Dozens of them, in neat rows.

The team spent eight weeks freeing the skull from the rock, working with tiny needles so they would not break a single feature.

Maya read the last paragraph twice. The scientists still did not agree on what the creature ate. Some said meat. Others said it swept the seafloor for shellfish.

"They just say they do not know," Maya said, surprised.

"That is the honest part," her teacher said. "Science means saying what you can prove and leaving the rest open."

transcript.title: How to Draw a Dinosaur
transcript.text:
The museum website had a lesson called How to Draw What a Dinosaur Looked Like.

Maya followed along with a pencil.

Step one was not the skin. It was the skeleton. "Start with what we actually know," the lesson said. "Bones are evidence. Everything else is a careful guess."

So Maya drew the spine first, curving like a bridge. Then the ribs, the long legs, the heavy tail held straight out for balance.

Step two was muscle. She thickened the thighs, because those bones had rough patches where muscle once gripped.

Step three was the fun part. Skin. Feathers. Color.

"Nobody knows the color," the lesson admitted. "Choose something an animal alive today might wear."

Maya made hers dark green with a pale stripe, like a lizard she had seen at the zoo.

She signed the corner: Maya, paleoartist.

Then she started another one.

chapters.title: Maya and the Stone Egg Case
chapters.text:
Maya came to the museum at nine. A stone case sat by the big bone frame. Inside the case was a huge dinosaur egg.

"What made this egg turn to stone?" Maya asked.

Dr. Pine gave her a smile. "Time," she said. "Mud and sand came over it. The shell took the shape of stone. Now we can hold it like a rock."

Maya took a close look. The egg had fine lines on its face. A thin crack made a wide shape, like a smile.

"Can I take a note?" Maya asked.

Dr. Pine gave her a page and a pen. Maya wrote: This egg is the size of a plate. It has a shine in the lamp light.

Dr. Pine said that scientists still find fresh dinosaur facts and new art every year. Maya wrote that down too.

"I like this job," Maya said. "Same time next week?"

transcript.title: The Paleoart Show
transcript.text:
Maya taped eleven drawings to the hallway wall and called it a show.

Grandpa came. Jean came. Even Eesa came, holding a juice box.

Maya walked them along the wall like a museum guide.

"This one is a Stegosaurus. The plates might have been for showing off, not fighting. Scientists argue about it."

"This one has feathers. Lots of dinosaurs did. Birds are dinosaurs, actually."

Jean squinted. "Birds are dinosaurs?"

"The only ones left," Maya said. "Everything else disappeared. But the pigeon on your roof is a cousin of the T. rex."

Eesa looked at his juice box and then out the window, worried.

At the end of the hallway was a blank sheet of paper and a cup of pencils.

"Your turn," Maya said. "Draw the skeleton first. Then guess the rest, like a real paleoartist."

Everyone sat down on the floor.

chapters.title: Maya and the Bone Shape Puzzle
chapters.text:
Maya came to the museum with a note in her hand. The note said: five bones, one shape, one name.

A scientist named Jade gave Maya a wide tray. "These bones came from a dig site," she said. "Take your time and make the shape fit."

Maya made a line with the first bone. The next bone was the same size, so she made it fit beside the first. The third bone had a fine curve like a smile.

"That spine is huge," Maya said. "What kind of dinosaur is this?"

Jade smiled. "Kids who read dinosaur news can name it."

Maya put the last bone in place. The shape made a long tail and a big plate. "A Stegosaurus!" she said.

Jade gave her a shiny pin. It made a bright shine in the museum lights.

"Come back next week," Jade said. "We have a new case of bones to name."
